The closest match is Seed-Guided Semi-Supervised Clustering by A-Contrario Anomaly Detection, which explicitly uses minimal user-provided labels to start groups and then expands them by admitting non-anomalous points, in an iterative “clustering-by-exclusion” scheme that isolates outliers and fringe points [1]. It fits your description of identifying clusters by removing odd ones out using a few starting markers [1].

A related but less direct option is the outlier-detection paper based on cluster analysis and visual expert criteria, which also treats outliers as points identified after clustering, but it is not seed-guided clustering [7].
